summary.headline: Fedbank Q2 FY27: PAT rose 63% YoY to INR130.8 crore and ROA hit a record 2.8%, but GNPA rose to 1.8% on gold-loan repayment-model transition.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter on profitability: PAT of INR130.8 crore (up 14.3% QoQ, 63% YoY), ROA of 2.8% and ROE of 17%, both records. AUM grew 37% YoY to INR22,035 crore, with gold AUM up 77% YoY to INR11,917 crore. Management attributed the rise in GNPA (1.6% to 1.8%) and Stage II (2.7% to 3.6%) mainly to the shift from bullet to periodic interest-due gold loans, which it called technical. Management flagged intense gold-loan competition in Q2 and said it would keep growing and guiding for Q3 and Q4.

financial_highlights.value: INR27.1 crore (~0.6% of avg total assets, annualised)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA up from 1.6% in Q1; both improved YoY

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR5,822 crore (+31% YoY); AUM INR11,917 crore (+77% YoY); LTV 68%; gold tonnage +16% YoY; 74 branches added taking gold branch count to 831; AUM per branch INR16.9 crore. Doorstep gold AUM INR1,851 crore. Entered Eastern India this quarter.

segments.name: Mortgage (LAP and housing)
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR855 crore (+12% YoY); AUM INR9,982 crore (+13.5% YoY). Medium-ticket LAP disbursed INR645 crore (+16% YoY) at 11.5-12.5% yield. Small-ticket LAP and housing disbursed INR210 crore; management said credit costs on ST LAP are now normalising and approval rates have risen to mid-40% from about 30%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% for FY27, unchanged; management said this holds even with flat gold prices, assuming around 10-12% annual tonnage growth.
ROA target of 3% and ROE of about 18%; ROA is the primary guided metric. FY26 ROA was about 2.4%, with a guided 30-40 bps improvement.
Credit cost guided to stay well below 1%; GNPA guided below 2%.
Plans for at least 150 more branches in H2 FY27 and about 100 gold branches; cost-to-income expected to rise only modestly despite investment opex.
Management said H2 is seasonally stronger, with tonnage growth expected in Q3 and Q4, and ST LAP disbursements expected to pick up in Q3 and Q4.

Management declined to give NIM or yield guidance for Q3, saying it would use yield, LTV and growth levers together. It also said some rate-hike pass-through will be limited and absorbed by opex and credit cost levers.
capex_capacity: 74 gold branches opened in Q2, taking the total to 831; at least 150 more planned in H2 FY27, with about 100 gold branches cited.
A new branch reaches INR6-7 crore AUM and turns profitable in about 12-13 months, per management; about 150 branches were added last year and most reportedly followed this path.
Opex as a share of average total assets was 4.9% in Q2 vs 4.8% in Q1 and 5.5% in FY26, reflecting full-quarter branch and headcount costs.
AUM per gold branch rose from INR8 crore to INR16 crore (cited in the Q&A); management said cost-to-income should fall as AUM per branch grows.
demand_pricing: Gold-loan competition was heightened in Q2 across geographies, with NBFCs using yield, LTV and lending-practice strategies. Gold yield fell about 10 bps over Q1 and Q2 combined, per management. Management said bank competition is in a different yield segment.

Gold LTV is 68% overall; customers take the maximum LTV available (75-80% in most cases), and the portfolio has a mix of 71-74%. Income-generating loans (about 20% of disbursements) are priced on cash flow with LTV caps of 75-85%.
ST LAP origination yield has fallen from 16.1% to 14.9% over 5-6 quarters; management attributed this to state mix and competition, not ticket size, and said yields should improve in Q3.
Approval rates in ST LAP have recovered to mid-40% from about 30% after BRE tightening.
Medium-ticket LAP is partner-driven, runs at 11.5-12.5% yield, and is a steady, profitable business.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage gold loan growth and yields given rising competition from NBFCs and banks? Is an income-generating loan product ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 competition was the most intense yet, and it chose a balance of growth and yield. Gold yield fell only about 10 bps across Q1 and Q2. The IGL product has been live since April, with LTV structured at 75-85% based on cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Stage II and III rises in gold: is this the new normal, and will it deteriorate further in Q3-Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Stage II rise technical, since most gold loans are 2.5-3 month tenor products and customers are moving to periodic interest. It said the change could take 1-2 more quarters to settle, and it declined to give a Stage II number. CFO said there have been no auction losses in six years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ST LAP yields fall, and how much will they rise with rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to state mix, not ticket size, and said Q3 yields will be higher than Q2 with higher disbursements. ST LAP ticket sizes have moved up to INR7-8 lakh, with a minimum of INR8 lakh now.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 AUM and ROE guidance be raised given H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept AUM growth guidance at 20-25% for FY27 and said ROE could see upside. Target is ROA 3% and ROE about 18%. Management said upside depends on gold prices.

qa_highlights.question: How will rate hikes affect spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said pass-through will be limited, with the company absorbing part of the shock. Offsets will come from opex and credit cost. Fixed-rate borrowings are 33%, MCLR-linked 24%, and about 58% of the loan book is short-tenor gold loans that reprice at maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for the mortgage business and its ROA as mix shifts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold ROA will be maintained, not expanded, as AUM per branch rises and cost-to-income falls. ST LAP ROA is expected to move toward gold ROA over time, and the gold mix will not drop in the next cycle.

risks_watch: Gold GNPA 1.8% and Stage II 3.6%: management says the rise is technical, but next quarter needs to show whether it has stabilised.
Gold-loan competition: Q2 was heightened and management expects Q3 to be intense too, so yields and LTV could come under pressure.
Rate hikes: management said pass-through will be limited; borrowing cost is 7.80% and fixed-rate share is 33%.
Opex: at least 150 more branches in H2 could push cost-to-income up despite the stated aim to contain it.
ST LAP recovery: H2 growth and yield recovery depend on the Q3 pickup, and disbursements were only INR210 crore in Q2.
Gold prices were flat; AUM guidance of 20-25% depends on tonnage growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and the ROA trajectory, but cautious on gold yields and asset quality. Management was guarded on Stage II and yield outlook, declining to give numbers and calling the gap technical; it stood firm on credit cost, AUM and ROA guidance.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 '27 has been our strongest quarter to date in terms of profitability and operating metrics.
We have never had an auction loss on either principal or interest in the last 6 years.
The Stage II, we think, is in a managed range.
Our target ROA we are trying to reach is 3% and correspondingly try and touch an 18% ROE.

adds.what: At least 150 more gold/lending branches planned in H2 FY27 (about 100 of them gold branches)

growth.why: Management held FY27 AUM growth guidance at 20-25% (midpoint 22.5%), backed by at least 150 more branches in H2 FY27 and H2 tonnage growth of 10-12%, though no order-book style numbers were given for growth and gold competition is intense.
